newsitem.title: UK: No casualties in attack on N.Ireland police patrol.
newsitem.headline: No casualties in attack on N.Ireland police patrol.

text.p: A bomb attack was launched on a police patrol in north Belfast late on Thursday, Northern Ireland security sources said.
There were no reports of any injuries, the sources added.
First reports said a grenade of a type often used by IRA guerrillas had been fired at an armoured police vehicle but it was not known if it hit the vehicle.
"There was an attack on a police mobile patrol at Limestone Road," a security source said. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

The attack occurred just 36 hours after British Prime Minister Tony Blair launched an initiative aimed at persuading the Irish Republican Army (IRA) to abandon its long guerrilla war against British rule in Northern Ireland and to secure a place at peace talks.
